_comment: Plain-language wording for the axe-core rules we run. axe does the detecting; these texts explain the result to non-specialists.

tabindex.title: Positive tabindex changes the Tab order
tabindex.why: A tabindex above 0 pulls an element ahead of everything else, so keyboard users jump around the page instead of moving through it in reading order.
tabindex.fix: Remove the tabindex (or set it to 0) and move the element in the HTML to where it should be reached.
tabindex.note: axe treats this as a best practice. It becomes a WCAG failure when the resulting order is confusing, which it usually is.

heading-order.title: Heading levels are skipped
heading-order.why: Screen reader users jump between headings to scan a page. A jump such as H1 to H4 suggests missing sections and makes the outline harder to follow.
heading-order.fix: Use the next level down (H2 after H1, H3 after H2). Choose the level for structure and use CSS for the size.
heading-order.note: A best practice, not a WCAG failure on its own.

page-has-heading-one.title: No H1 heading
page-has-heading-one.why: An H1 naming the page lets screen reader users confirm where they are and jump straight to the main content.
page-has-heading-one.fix: Add one H1 with the page title at the start of the main content.
page-has-heading-one.note: A best practice, not a WCAG failure on its own.

empty-heading.title: Empty heading
empty-heading.why: A heading with no text is announced as just 'heading', which tells screen reader users nothing.
empty-heading.fix: Give the heading text, or remove the heading markup if it is only used for spacing or styling.

bypass.title: No way to skip repeated content
bypass.why: Without a skip link, landmarks or headings, keyboard and screen reader users must go through the whole header and menu on every page.
bypass.fix: Add a 'Skip to main content' link as the first item on the page, and mark up the page with <header>, <nav> and <main>.

scrollable-region-focusable.title: Scrollable area may not be reachable by keyboard
scrollable-region-focusable.why: Keyboard users scroll a box by focusing it. Chrome and Firefox now make such boxes focusable automatically; Safari does not, so there it cannot be scrolled without a mouse.
scrollable-region-focusable.fix: Add tabindex="0" to the scrolling box and give it a name (for example aria-label="Terms and conditions") so it works in every browser.

frame-focusable-content.title: Frame with focusable content is removed from the Tab order
frame-focusable-content.why: The frame has tabindex="-1", so keyboard users cannot reach the links or controls inside it.

region.title: Content outside landmarks
region.why: Screen reader users jump between landmarks (header, navigation, main, footer) to get around. Content outside any landmark is easy to miss.
region.fix: Put all content inside a landmark: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <aside> or <footer>, or a <section> with a heading or aria-label.
region.note: A best practice, not a WCAG failure on its own.

landmark-one-main.title: No main landmark
landmark-one-main.why: A main landmark lets keyboard and screen reader users jump straight to the page content.
landmark-one-main.fix: Wrap the page content in a single <main> element.
landmark-one-main.note: A best practice, not a WCAG failure on its own.
